query: Consider the following context: Noble metal–based high-entropy alloys (NM-HEAs) are promising catalysts because of their diverse compositions and complex surface structures, although understanding their formation and achieving precise atomic control remain challenging. In that context, which method can be used for produce HEA three-dimensional nanoframeworks, and why?

decision.trend: The trend in the research on high-entropy alloys (HEAs) is focused on understanding their microstructure, mechanical properties, and potential applications. Recent studies have explored the effects of different processing routes, alloy compositions, and environmental conditions on the properties of HEAs. The development of new synthesis methods, such as selective laser melting (SLM) and spark plasma sintering (SPS), has enabled the creation of HEAs with unique microstructures and improved properties.
decision.unsolved: One of the remaining challenges in the field of HEAs is the lack of precise control over their atomic structure and composition, which can lead to variability in their properties. Additionally, the high configurational entropy of HEAs can result in complex phase transitions and microstructural evolution, which are not yet fully understood.
decision.why: In-situ TEM can provide real-time observations of the microstructural evolution of HEAs under various environmental conditions, enabling a deeper understanding of their phase transitions, defect formation, and property changes. This can help to overcome the current limitations in controlling the atomic structure and composition of HEAs, and can inform the development of new synthesis methods and processing routes.
